newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares finish stronger in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares finish stronger in thin trading.

text.p: There was little trading on the Nigerian stock exchange on Monday as a Christmas holiday mood came early to the floor, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 6,978.85 from 6,972.20 on Friday on modest price gains in the oil and banking sectors.
"Many traders have closed for the year and activities will reduce progressively as the year grinds to an end," one said. "Not much business will be done between now and the new year."
Oil marketing shares dominated activities, recording most of the gains of the day.
Unipetrol was the leading stock at 58.05 naira, up 30 kobo. Total rose 15 kobo to 57.30 naira while National Oil finished 17 kobo more at 46.80 naira.
Union Bank closed 20 kobo higher at 5.70 naira on renewed demand following what brokers said was the mopping up of excess shares arising from the bank's last bonus issue.
United Bank for Africa finished five kobo stronger at 5.90 naira on investors positive perception.
Lever Brothers shares were unchanged at 20.40 naira, after it reported profit after tax for January-September was one billion naira against 1.1 billion naira in the same period of 1995.
Managing director Rufus Giwa said in a statement the result was "an improvement over that of March and June quarters."
PZ industries, which posted an improved first quarter result to end-August 1996, was static because of a freeze on its price pending the conclusion of a merger exercise.
After-tax profit for the quarter was 316.8 million naira from 267.8 million naira in the same period last year.
Monday's sole loser was Cadbury, which closed 40 kobo lower at 21.70 naira because of a large chunk of its stock on sale.
